disagreement_records.old: Reported results (source excerpt): In simulation, TDMPC2 demonstrates a significantly higher mean success rate than SAC (58%vs.36%,p <0.001), and mean tip contact forces of0.15 N, well below the proposed1.5 Nvessel rupture threshold. Mean success rates for TD-MPC2 (68%) were comparable to SAC (60%)in vitro, but TD-MPC2 achieved superior path ratios (p= 0.017) at the cost of longer procedure times (p <0.001).
disagreement_records.proposed: Higher simulated success 58±50% versus 36±48%, p<0.001, with longer overall time and higher force summaries. Physical success 68±48% versus 60±50%, p=0.567, does not establish equivalence. A2L path ratio 71±14% versus 47±11%, p=0.017; both have zero A2L success. Proposed force reference does not establish tissue safety.

scope_choices: Automated model review, not independent human verification or replication.
This synthesis read all seven supplied text pages and earlier image-review notes. Original page images were not directly supplied to this call.
Source path/hash and upstream call receipts are supplied provenance, not newly verified filesystem/API facts. No external cited paper, repository, raw data or supplement was accessed.
Batch-local statements in earlier page notes about unavailable other pages are not global source gaps: their combined coverage spans all seven pages.
All 128 catalogue features receive main-model dispositions. Auxiliary SAC and external-physics scopes are selectively assessed, not claimed separately exhaustive.
Raw evidence preserves extracted table row-merging artifacts. Structured table-cell separation also uses supplied upstream image transcriptions, not direct image reinspection here.
Implemented scope is separately initialized first-phase navigation, not continuous complete thrombectomy, clot retrieval, reperfusion or patient treatment.
CTA-derived anatomical holdouts have simulated navigation outcomes and do not establish held-out actual human clinical transition/outcome validation for R2/R3.
One physical phantom uses a simulation-training anatomy. Phantom control supports R1, not unseen physical-anatomy validation or R6.
An expert's informal testbed experience is human involvement but does not establish a defined model-output evaluation or R4.
Shared lower anatomy, ten training/five held-out upper geometries, predominantly Type-I arches and one phantom restrict generalization and independence.
Rigid empty vessels, incomplete material/friction calibration, unreported tracking errors, coordinate calibration, target tolerance and radiation dose limit safety interpretation.

Transition network, dimension, losses, stochasticity, pretrained parameters, useful history length, candidate count, prediction depth and exact replanning settings remain unreported; cited systems' capabilities are not inherited.
Implemented transitions/evaluated L4 decisions are distinct from unreported standalone predictive fidelity and a separate L3 matched-alternative experiment.
Training budget and earlier result checkpoints are preserved separately. Selection, seeds, pairing, clustering and multiplicity controls remain unclear.
Procedure time conditions on success and path ratio on failure. Algorithms/environments can therefore use different subsets; aggregate weighting and backtracking calculations are unclear.
Episode caps, physical pauses, exploration iterations and prediction horizon are separate. The 0.5 s pause is not inference latency.
Force maxima average episode maxima, not the greatest instantaneous force. The proposed cited 1.5 N reference is not validated here as a tissue/device-specific or universal clinical threshold.
Physical wall-force sensing is future work. Simulated logging, speed bounds and timeouts do not establish comprehensive protection or absence of injury.
Anomalous dispersions, inconsistent failure denominators and prose/table reversals are retained and queued without replacement values.
Nonsignificance is not equivalence; the SAC-only augmentation ablation does not isolate TD-MPC2 dynamics/planning.
Physical mismatch testing does not isolate model exploitation or validate clinical causal effects.
Open-source dependencies and manuscript CC BY do not establish study-specific code, weight, configuration or data release/licenses.
No gate pass, safety guarantee or deployment authorization is asserted.
No files were saved and no executable schema, graph, quotation or semantic validation was run.
